title: Ingest pipeline observability guardrails and adaptive alerting playbook
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a concrete playbook to instrument the analytics ingest pipeline (Console backend -> analytics ingress -> stream processors -> long-term storage) with production-grade SLIs/SLOs, trace/log enrichment, cost-conscious retention and adaptive alerting. The goal is to detect degradations earlier, reduce alert fatigue, and provide deterministic remediation steps for engineers and SREs while keeping telemetry costs bounded.

Scope:
- Define SLIs and SLOs for ingest: request success rate, end-to-end ingest latency (90/99p), consumer lag, pipeline processing throughput, and data completeness (drop rate).
- Tracing strategy: span design for ingest entry/exit, partitioning keys, backpressure signals, and cross-service correlation through request_id and trace_id propagation.
- Logging: structured JSON logs with schema, log-level guidelines (rate-limited ERRORs), and retention tiers.
- Dashboards: Grafana boards for golden signals, per-tenant views, and an anomaly timeline.
- Adaptive alerting: circuit-breaker based alert thresholds, dynamic baselining for noisy tenants, and cost-aware sampling to keep observability spend within budgets.
- Runbooks and on-call playbook for common failure modes.

Acceptance criteria:
- SLIs defined and stored in the SLO registry for ingest pipeline with clear ownership and alert rules.
- Tracing implemented for the ingest edge and first-stage stream processors with <1% trace loss and consistent trace_id propagation.
- Dashboards published: "Ingest Health", "Latency Heatmap", "Per-Tenant Drop Rates" and linked from Console.
- Adaptive alerting prototype that adjusts thresholds based on rolling 14-day baselines and suppresses low-severity alerts for tenants under quota.
- Cost-aware sampling policies implemented (prefix caching, deterministic sampling for critical paths).
- Runbook covering the top 5 incident scenarios added to internal runbooks with postmortem checklist.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Sampling: we prefer deterministic sampling (e.g., hash-based per-tenant skirts) for traces so important sessions are always captured. This reduces visibility noise but risks missing rare cascading failures; mitigated by synthetic probes and targeted 100% tracing during rollouts.
- SLO targets: Use medium-tier SLOs for aggregate metrics (e.g., 99.9% ingest success rate) and per-tenant SLOs for paying customers where we can measure and enforce. Per-tenant SLOs increase cardinality; we will roll out per-tenant trends only for top-500 tenants to keep query costs constrained.
- Alerting: Implement multi-window alerts (short high-severity window + long lower-severity window) to reduce paging on transient spikes.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) 2026-02-24: Define SLI formulas and register them (owner: Observability team).
2) 2026-03-03: Instrument tracing at ingress, include trace_id/request_id middleware (PR #2341).
3) 2026-03-10: Deploy structured logging schema and ship log enrichment library.
4) 2026-03-17: Launch dashboards and SLO-based alerts in lower environments.
5) 2026-03-24: Enable adaptive alerting experiment for 10% of traffic.
6) 2026-04-01: Full rollout and runbook sign-off.

Instrumentation specifics:
- Traces: Use sample priority tags; ensure KV cache budget tags flow into spans. Annotate spans with tenant_id, model_variant, route_id, and batch_size.
- Logs: Include run_id and ingestion_partition in every log line. Use structured error codes to enable quick aggregation.
- Metrics: Histogram buckets for token-level and request-level latencies, and gauge for consumer_lag. Emit ingest_batch_size and process_time per shard.

Alerting policy (prototype):
- P0: End-to-end ingest latency 99p > 2x SLO for >5m. Page on-call, trigger failover.
- P1: Success rate < SLO - 0.5% for >10m. Notify channel + runbook.
- P2: Consumer lag > threshold for >30m. Pager only if leads to data loss.
Adaptive rules: suppress alerts for tenants flagged as "low priority"; escalate if suppression correlates with increased drop rate.

Rollout & QA:
- Start in staging with synthetic load generator (ingest-prober) to validate SLO computation and alerting.
- Canary rollout to 10% traffic with 100% tracing. Compare per-window baseline deltas before expanding.
- Define QA checklist: ingestion correctness, trace linkage checks, log schema validation, dashboard visual verification.

Risks and mitigations:
- High cardinality cost (per-tenant traces/metrics): mitigate by tiered retention and sampling; store high-cardinality indices only for top tenants.
- False positives from noisy metrics: use rolling baselines + anomaly suppression rules.
- Missing traces during outages: ensure synthetic probes run from multiple regions and add 100% trace capture during incident mode.

Next steps / action items:
- Marcus to open tracing middleware PR and link to this ticket (PR #2341).
- Observability lead (Priya) to finalize SLI formulas and SLO thresholds by 2026-02-24.
- Infra to reserve a metrics-query budget and set retention tiers.

Notes:
This playbook is intended to be executable by on-call engineers and product SREs; it should live alongside the Console SLO registry and be linked from the Console runbooks page.
